title.narrative: Central Asia Regional Economic Cooperation Regional Improving Border Services Project

description.narrative: The proposed project will (i) improve border crossing point infrastructure and facility at Torkham, Chaman, and Wagha to the standard that meets users' demand for quality border crossing services; and (ii) establish a border point management regime and enhance knowledge and skills of border point operating agencies.

title.narrative: Reports and Recommendations of the President

description.narrative: Output/s as listed by the project staff.

Output: Border crossing point infrastructure and facilities at Chaman, Torkham, and Wagha improved Indicator: Border point facilities certified as compliant to internationally accepted standards at Chaman, Torkham, and Wagha by 2025 Achievement: N Progress/Status: BCP Torkham - CW contract awarded on 20 December 2018. Physical progress at 98.67% as of December 2025. BCP Chaman - CW contract awarded on 20 August 2019. Physical progress at 97.84% as of December 2025. BCP Wagha - FBR requested EAD for the removal of the BCP from the project scope due to insufficient funds under the loan. ADB's decision is pending. Data Source: Project progress report and project completion report Baseline year: 2013 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2013 Baseline value: N Target year: 2025 Target value: Y Actual value: N

Output: Governance structure of national border point management regime produced and adopted; and organizational design, management structure, financial and administrative procedures, and financial modeling for the PLPA produced and adopted Indicator: PLPA established with transparent governance structure and clear vision and mandate statement by 2025 Achievement: N Progress/Status: The consulting contract for the PLPA establishment, institutional development and technical support was awarded on 29 December 2020 with a completion date of 30 June 2023. Due to the additional tasks and the government delays with the PLPA establishment, the contract completion date was extended twice up to 30 December 2024. The draft PLPA Act, one of the key deliverables under the contract and the critical step to establishing the PLPA organization, has been tabled in the National Assembly for legislation and expected for approval by Q1 2025. The PLPA consulting contract has been extended until 30 December 2025 to support the PLPA establishment activities which will be required after the PLPA Act approval. Data Source: Project progress report and project completion report Baseline year: 2013 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2013 Baseline value: N Target year: 2025 Target value: Y Actual value: N

Output: Knowledge and skills of border point operating agencies enhanced Indicator: Professionally qualified border point agencies and officials appointed by 2025 Achievement: N Progress/Status: The EA put on hold the procurement of consulting services for training and capacity development of border point operating agencies and proposed to remove this from the project scope because similar training activities can be sourced from other international development partners on a grant financing basis.
